## What does a productive error look like?

Here's a real one, from AI weather forecasting: how the model failed, what the
failure revealed, and what science gained. Scroll, or press Run, to step
through it.
:::
:::

<!-- Cells 3–5: the FourCastNet → SFNO case, as told in O'Loughlin et al. 2025
(Sect. 4.2), citing Pathak et al. 2022 and Bonev et al. 2023. -->

::: {.notebook-cell .code-cell tabindex="0" data-cell="3" role="group" aria-label="Cell 3"}
::: {.cell-prompt}
<span class="prompt-label" aria-hidden="true"></span><button type="button" class="run-cell" aria-label="Run cell 3"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M4 2.5v11l9-5.5z"/></svg></button>
:::

::: {.code-input}
<code><span class="code-function">forecast</span>(<span class="code-variable">ai_weather_model</span>, <span class="code-variable">days</span><span class="code-operator">=</span><span class="code-number">365</span>)</code>
:::

::: {.cell-output .error-output}
[InstabilityError]{.error-name}: forecast unstable beyond 10 days

FourCastNet, an AI weather model built on Fourier neural operators, made fast,
skillful short-range forecasts. But a numerical instability kept it to
forecasts shorter than ten days.

<figure class="globe-figure">
<div class="globes" role="img" aria-label="Animation: two spinning globes. On the left, real weather patterns evolve smoothly. On the right, the AI model's forecast develops a star-shaped pattern of errors around the south pole that grows until the forecast breaks down around day 10.">
<div class="globe"><span class="globe-disc"><canvas data-model="truth"></canvas></span><span class="globe-label">Real weather</span></div>
<div class="globe"><span class="globe-disc"><canvas data-model="flat"></canvas></span><span class="globe-label">AI model</span></div>
</div>
<div class="globe-controls">
<span class="globe-day" aria-hidden="true">Day 0</span>
<button type="button" class="nb-tool globe-toggle">Pause</button>
</div>
<figcaption>Watch the south pole. The model's flat-map math fits a round planet worst at the poles, so its errors start there.</figcaption>
<div class="cell-source">Illustration inspired by <a href="https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/bonev23a.html">Bonev et al. 2023</a>, Fig. 4; not output from the models.</div>
</figure>
:::
:::

::: {.notebook-cell .code-cell tabindex="0" data-cell="4" role="group" aria-label="Cell 4"}
::: {.cell-prompt}
<span class="prompt-label" aria-hidden="true"></span><button type="button" class="run-cell" aria-label="Run cell 4"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M4 2.5v11l9-5.5z"/></svg></button>
:::

::: {.code-input}
<code><span class="code-function">diagnose</span>(<span class="code-variable">error</span>)</code>
:::

::: {.output-prompt aria-hidden="true"}
:::

::: {.cell-output}
**It assumed the Earth was flat.**

Researchers traced the problem to one component, the Fourier transform. Its
math describes a flat sheet that wraps around at the edges, and it handles the
poles badly. Replacing it with spherical harmonics, the sphere's version of the
same math, gave a model that stayed stable for a full year of simulated
weather.

<figure class="forecast-chart">
<figcaption>How far ahead each model could forecast before becoming unstable (to scale)</figcaption>
<div class="bar-row">
<span class="bar-label"><strong>Under 10 days</strong> · FourCastNet, flat Fourier transforms</span>
<span class="bar-track" aria-hidden="true"><span class="bar bar-before"></span></span>
</div>
<div class="bar-row">
<span class="bar-label"><strong>1 year</strong> · rebuilt with spherical harmonics</span>
<span class="bar-track" aria-hidden="true"><span class="bar bar-after"></span></span>
</div>
</figure>

::: {.cell-source}
Sources: [Pathak et al. 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.11214), FourCastNet;
[Bonev et al. 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/bonev23a.html),
*Spherical Fourier Neural Operators*, ICML;
[O'Loughlin et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-18-787-2025),
*Geoscientific Model Development*, Sect. 4.2.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notebook-cell .code-cell tabindex="0" data-cell="5" role="group" aria-label="Cell 5"}
::: {.cell-prompt}
<span class="prompt-label" aria-hidden="true"></span><button type="button" class="run-cell" aria-label="Run cell 5"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M4 2.5v11l9-5.5z"/></svg></button>
:::

::: {.code-input}
<code><span class="code-function">learn_from</span>(<span class="code-variable">error</span>)</code>
:::

::: {.output-prompt aria-hidden="true"}
:::

::: {.cell-output}
The error didn't just get fixed. It left science better off:

- **Understanding.** Tracing the failure to one component showed how the
  model works, insight that explainability tools rarely provide.
- **Antifragility.** The model came back stronger than before, stable for a
  year instead of ten days. Some systems gain from failure instead of merely
  surviving it.
- **Credibility.** By diagnosing the failure in the open, researchers showed
  they understood a system that is hard to see inside.

**Most discussions of AI in science ask how to eliminate errors. We ask what
errors teach.**

::: {.cell-source}
Sources: [O'Loughlin 2023](https://doi.org/10.1007/s13194-023-00522-z) and
[O'Loughlin et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-18-787-2025) on
understanding; Taleb 2012, *Antifragile*, on antifragility;
[Mayernik 2021](https://doi.org/10.17351/ests2021.769) on credibility.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notebook-cell .code-cell tabindex="0" data-cell="6" role="group" aria-label="Cell 6"}
::: {.cell-prompt}
<span class="prompt-label" aria-hidden="true"></span><button type="button" class="run-cell" aria-label="Run cell 6"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M4 2.5v11l9-5.5z"/></svg></button>
:::

::: {.code-input}
<code><span class="code-function">why_it_matters</span>()</code>
:::

::: {.output-prompt aria-hidden="true"}
:::

::: {.cell-output}
AI models are moving into everyday science. Since February 2025, the European
Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts has run an AI forecast model
operationally, alongside its physics-based one.

Climate is harder still. The future climate lies outside any data a model was
trained on, so it can't simply be checked against observations.

**Knowing how these models fail, and what their failures reveal, is how
scientists will know when to trust them.**

::: {.cell-source}
Source: [ECMWF 2025](https://www.ecmwf.int/en/about/media-centre/news/2025/ecmwfs-ai-forecasts-become-operational),
"ECMWF's AI forecasts become operational".
:::
:::
:::

We're talking with the people who build and use these models: scientists,
software engineers and data specialists at NSF NCAR, NASA GISS and Columbia
University's LEAP Center. We also read the reports, code and data records
where errors get written down.
